checks: Preparation binds the exact adapter SHA and current supported shapes.
Quality boundaries must all share one eleven-request client envelope; repeated question rows do not create eleven copies of one batch I/O delta.
History enumerates the frozen seven-position sequence across three rounds, retaining round and position; matrix enumerates six contexts with three separate client envelopes each.
Every started group must have terminal evidence before any raw resource stream is read, even when an earlier subset is selected.
A valid speed-only NO_GO permits offline inspection; each selected service group still needs passing HTTP, identity and cleanup contracts.
JSON metadata is decoded on its first bind and cached for later consumers; source signatures and SHA are retained and signatures rechecked after the bounded read.
PID generation, cgroup path, protocol axis, runtime/tool identity and runner/controller/client time containment are explicit gates.
PID read_bytes/rchar, cgroup I/O and whole-device counters are reported separately. Device traffic is not attributed wholly to q4t, and disk parents are never added to partitions.
Sampled memory.current peak and retained memory.peak are distinct, with their individual differences from memory.max retained.
NVIDIA, RSS, cgroup and file-cache observations are overlapping views; their independent peaks are not added into physical RAM.
Absent/unknown counters and wall-clock drift remain explicit rather than becoming zero, and 54GB physical union remains INDETERMINATE.
scope_limits: No immutable core arithmetic or its prior eight examples were rerun or newly certified.
An HTTP/evidence-failed service group is refused by this adapter rather than silently counted as covered; separate failure evidence remains necessary.
Metadata stat stability plus read-time SHA is a trusted-workspace integrity check, not a defense against adversarial same-stat file replacement.
Client envelopes include client launch/teardown and are not exact HTTP-only intervals.
Root must release explicit completed groups after active HTTP has ended; the preparation invocation is an example, not automatic authorization.
